bullets.title: S&P +1% to 7,730; Nasdaq +1.1%; market rallies on oil decline and Xi visit anticipation
bullets.body: S&P 500 futures rose ~0.7% to 7,761 and Nasdaq 100 +1.1% premarket as Brent crude fell ~2% to $101.77/bbl and markets anticipated a positive Trump-Xi summit (Sept 23-25). VIX at 14.75; 10-year yield eased ~5bps to 4.95%. S&P gamma backdrop positive post-monthly OPEX; dealer flows suppressing volatility with 10Y below 5% and WTI below $100.

bullets.title: Fed Goolsbee: 2% inflation target still achievable but 'won't be painless'; no ambiguity on hiking if demand overheats
bullets.body: Chicago Fed's Goolsbee said supply shocks are having persistent inflation impact, the credible path back to 2% is 'hard to see,' and rate cuts require convincing evidence inflation is fading. He stressed 'no ambiguity' about tightening if demand overheats and affirmed Fed independence as essential against political pressure for cheaper borrowing costs. Strong demand, energy prices, and tariffs all cited as concurrent inflation drivers.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley expects two more Fed hikes; mid-cycle rotation toward quality/asset-light equities
bullets.body: MS's macro forum flagged slower disinflation into 2027 due to oil pressures, with S&P forward P/E de-rating to 19x while earnings remain mid-teens growth. Leadership is rotating toward quality, services, and asset-light companies; MS YE S&P target 8,000 with 7,000-7,100 tactical downside if energy/midterm risks materialize. Treasury market pricing <25% recession risk but >75% aggregate demand shock risk.

bullets.title: Xi Jinping visits US Sept 23-25; China plans to drop 15% LNG tariff this week — trade thaw catalyst
bullets.body: China confirmed Xi's first US state visit in nearly three years, scheduled Sept 23-25 at the US president's invitation. Separately, China plans to remove its 15% tariff on US LNG this week, potentially reopening bilateral trade flows and enabling new deals. Markets flagged the visit as a positive catalyst for the tape.

bullets.title: Oil falls for 4th day on Iran diplomacy hopes and Saudi supply recovery; diesel at record $6.51/gal
bullets.body: WTI crude dropped ~2.8% to $93.37 on hopes for Iran diplomatic progress ahead of UN meetings and expectations Saudi shipments will partially recover. However, refined product prices diverged sharply: US diesel hit a record $6.51/gallon and regular gasoline approached $4.50, driven by Middle East disruption and Russian refinery constraints. JPMorgan's oil team reportedly abandoned Iran war scenario forecasting given policy unpredictability.

bullets.title: Hormuz Strait near-collapse: supertanker rates hit $1M+/day, only 17 vessels crossed over weekend
bullets.body: Supertanker rates on the Persian Gulf-to-China route surged to $1.035M/day, roughly 5x pre-war levels, as traffic through the Strait of Hormuz collapsed to just 17 commodity vessels over the weekend. Qatar said it could resume LNG operations within weeks of Hormuz reopening, and Houthi officials warned Egypt, Turkey, and Pakistan could be future targets.

bullets.title: Sec. 301 tariff legal challenge Sept 30: invalidation could trigger ~$100B refunds, bond market concern
bullets.body: The Court of International Trade will hear arguments Sept 30 on whether Trump's new Section 301 tariffs (10-12.5% on 60 economies, covering 99% of US imports, effective July 24) exceed legal authority. A similar IEEPA tariff invalidation generated ~$170B in refunds; the Sec. 301 equivalent is estimated at ~$100B. Projected $1 trillion in 10-year tariff revenue loss could pressure the bond market.

bullets.title: Semiconductor sector rips: AMD +9.2% to new 52-week high, ARM +14.2% on 156% unusual volume
bullets.body: AMD reached a new 52-week high at $611.13 (+9.2%, +287% YTD) and ARM surged 14.2% to $314.79 on 156% of average volume, with moves attributed to sector momentum and Muse AI read-throughs. SOX is trading at a 20% discount to the S&P at 13.6x forward P/E vs. a 5-year median of 20.5x; Morgan Stanley remains constructive on quality/AI adopter semis.

bullets.title: US data center power shortfall rises to 57GW gross by 2028 as Vera Rubin rack power jumps to 234kW
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's updated power analysis shows a 57 GW gross (33 GW net) US data center power shortfall through 2028, up from 38 GW prior, with 2029 adding another 68 GW of incremental demand. NVDA's Vera Rubin rack power is now estimated at 234 kW vs. 149 kW prior, and Rubin Ultra at 600 kW vs. 415 kW. Cost/TFLOP falls 94% from Hopper to Rubin Ultra, triggering Jevons paradox and higher aggregate electricity consumption.

bullets.title: Memory market tightening: DDR5 +5.3% M/M, DRAM modules +23.1% M/M; Nvidia sees chip demand doubling next year
bullets.body: Memory spot prices are rising sharply with DDR5 +5.3% M/M and DRAM modules +23.1% M/M as supply tightens. Nvidia's Jensen Huang projects the company will sell twice as many chips next year following 70% FY28 revenue guidance growth. Micron faces a Taiwan union strike threat over profit-sharing at its key DRAM/HBM plant; SK Hynix is exploring a potential US fab partnership with Intel.

bullets.title: AI capex unaffected by safety scrutiny; hyperscalers accumulated ~$300B off-balance-sheet AI guarantees TTM
bullets.body: Multiple sources confirm AI capex projections of $1T for 2026 and $1.6T for 2027 are unaffected by compute reallocation to safety and alignment. Hyperscalers have accumulated ~$300B in off-balance-sheet guarantees for AI projects over the trailing twelve months. AI safety scrutiny is seen as increasing compute/capex requirements, not derailing the infrastructure cycle. CIOs expect server/storage spending growth to reach all-time survey highs by 2027, with 70-75% pulling forward 2026 spend.

bullets.title: USD breakout is key macro shift; yen down 2.5% last week and declining further; gold/EM headwind
bullets.body: Hedgeye flagged the USD Index breaking out to Bullish TRADE and TREND as the key macro regime shift of the week. USD/JPY moved to Bullish TRADE; yen is down 2.5% vs. USD last week and falling again Monday morning. Dollar strength is a headwind for gold (approaching bearish TREND), silver (moved to bearish TREND), emerging markets, and bonds.

bullets.title: Bitcoin surges to $85K+, 8-month high; Ethereum also long on Bullish TRADE/TREND signals
bullets.body: Bitcoin climbed above $85,117, its highest level since January 29, up ~4% on the session and reaching an 8-month high. Hedgeye and other macro commentators remain long Bitcoin and Ethereum on bullish TRADE and TREND signals, though both are overbought in the immediate term and trimming is advised into strength rather than outright exit.

bullets.title: Profitable companies outperforming in Russell 2000 by ~500bps in 2026, reversing 2023 dynamic
bullets.body: Profitable Russell 2000 stocks are outperforming unprofitable ones by ~500 bps in 2026, a sharp reversal from 2023 when non-profitable names outperformed by 10 percentage points. The Russell 2000 contains 1,122 profitable (57%) and 782 unprofitable stocks. Russell 2000 is down 6.8% from its cycle peak and Hedgeye remains short.

bullets.title: Healthcare sector +12.7% over 3 months vs. Russell 2000 -4.0%; long/short spread generating significant alpha
bullets.body: Healthcare (XLV) is up 12.7% over the past three months, including +1.8% last week, while the Russell 2000 (IWM) is down 4.0% over the same period. At least one systematic framework is long healthcare and short small-cap as a 'Quad 2' regime trade generating substantial alpha.

bullets.title: OpenAI guides $36B 2026 revenues (+184% YoY); Anthropic completing 26% of company R&D end-to-end
bullets.body: OpenAI raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $36B from $30B, implying 184% YoY growth and accelerating Q3 sequential momentum to 51% QoQ from 18% in Q2. Separately, Anthropic disclosed Claude is completing 26% of company R&D end-to-end as of August 2026, and OpenAI is seen catching up meaningfully to Anthropic's capability lead. OpenAI projects negative FCF of ~$278B from 2026-2030.

bullets.title: NY RAISE Act requires large AI developers to publish safety frameworks and report critical incidents by Jan 2027
bullets.body: New York enacted the RAISE Act mandating large AI developers with $500M+ in revenue to publish safety frameworks and report critical safety incidents to the Department of Financial Services within 72 hours, effective January 1, 2027. The regulation adds compliance cost and disclosure obligations for major AI platform companies.

bullets.title: India 7.8% GDP growth with RBI expected to hike 25bps in October; equities rally running out of steam
bullets.body: India's Q2 2026 GDP grew 7.8% YoY (Q1 revised up to 8.6%), but core inflation is accelerating at its fastest quarterly pace since June 2023, prompting JPM to forecast a 25bp RBI hike at the October meeting. Near-term equity upside is capped by converging headwinds: crude oil spikes, RBI hiking, rising Fed rates, and a heavy IPO pipeline. JPM prefers mid/small-caps over large caps, with Nifty-50 base target 27,000.

bullets.title: Semiconductor customer inventory days rose to 58-day forward supply in 2Q26; yellow flag, not yet red
bullets.body: Semiconductor customer inventory forward days rose to 58 days (+4 days QoQ) in 2Q26, the third consecutive quarterly increase, though levels remain below the prior cycle peak. Strong data center demand is currently more important than rising inventory; analysts characterize this as a yellow flag but not yet a concern requiring defensive positioning.

bullets.title: 'Streamflation' accelerating cancellations: 39% of Americans dropped a streaming sub in 6 months vs. 29% in March
bullets.body: A new survey found 39% of Americans canceled at least one streaming subscription over the past six months, up sharply from 29% in March, driven by repeated price hikes and broader cost-of-living pressures including record diesel at $6.51/gal. The trend represents a structural headwind for the streaming sector.
